notes:
Three releases at once - the phone build was on 2.12.1 while the web ran ahead.

THE MINING SESSION. A live crew board. Start a session, share a link or an eight-character code, and crew join from a phone without an account. Work orders, your own refinery timers, a crew split and a settle-up, all shared live. Your private refinery order stays the only source of truth, so a load cannot be counted twice, and banked, estimated and cost money are three separate numbers that nothing sums. Alternate Seller lets one organised quartermaster keep the books for a crew who have installed nothing. Streamer Mode masks every handle and hides the join code behind a tap. An order pirates took is marked lost with a reason.

A NAME THAT IS YOURS. Claim a Mavin handle - it is unique, and once claimed it cannot be typed over, so a name on a crew board means something. Optionally prove the RSI account behind it: Mavin gives you a sentence to paste into your RSI bio and reads it back. Verified accounts carry a small RSI mark on the crew board, the fleet ops roster and in Social - the one thing beside a name that is not self-reported, because the server refuses it to anyone whose identity it did not record. Nobody will ever send you a Mavin code to paste; only paste a line you generated yourself. Claiming is permanent: there is no unclaim, and a claimed handle is 3-24 characters of letters, numbers, _ and -, so names with spaces or org tags cannot be claimed. The app asks before you do it.

FASTER, AND CLEARER ABOUT WHAT IT KNOWS. The Star Citizen price payload halved (1,339,939 bytes down to 675,150) and now revalidates instead of re-downloading. Prices carry their age, and where a number is modelled rather than measured it says so.

FIXED. A join code could not be created at all if your phone's clock ran a few seconds fast, and the app blamed it on not being signed in. The keyboard covered the fields on Preferences, RSI verification, the ship loadout editor and the Add-blueprint picker. The weekly cleanup of unused anonymous accounts was also deleting Discord accounts and signing returning players out - no data was lost. A multi-ore refining run wrote the whole refinery fee onto every one of its orders, so a three-ore run with a 180,000 aUEC fee reported 360,000 of expense in your own books.

DATA. Star Citizen 4.10.0 hotfix (changelist 12568521). No reference values changed from 4.10.0 - the maths and every number are the same; only the stamps moved.
